floor_history.headline: Recon mapped the whole 18-diff gap to 3 mechanisms and closed 14 of them in pure C: floor 18 -> 4 (split-init address accumulation, a shared named static-pointer carrier, and a pre-loop `last = 3` tha

Floor 4 -> 2 and build_insns 134 -> 133 (== target): H4 CLOSED by deleting the arg1 alias and one hop of the end_off carrier chain TOGETHER; H5 (the Case3 `move a1,zero` placement) killed on every C-l

Floor held at 2/133; the last three C-level structural axes (dispatch shape, loop shape, dependence height) are KILLED with measurements, and a sibling counter-example proves our own toolchain emits t

frontier.hypothesis: The `move a1,zero` placement is decided by rank_for_schedule inside sched1, and the deciding quantity is the a1 set-up's own INSN_PRIORITY (or whether it is in the ready list at that step) - not the address chain's height, which s3 measured dead.
frontier.mechanism: Backward list scheduling places `sw p_static` first (it ends up immediately before the jal); at the next step ours picks the a1 set-up and target's build picks the address chain. Priority is compared before both tiebreaks, and both tiebreaks favour a1.
frontier.next_probe: Run cc1 with the build flags plus -da on the sandbox's preprocessed file and read the .sched dump for the Case3 block: record the actual INSN_PRIORITY of the a1 set-up and of the lui/addiu/sw chain. Cheaper still, set BB2_RANK_DEBUG=1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 is the instrumented binary) and read the RANKDBG line for that comparison directly.

frontier.hypothesis: The sibling func_8005D46C is the control experiment that answers it: same callee, same statement shape, same compiler, and our build gets the args-first order RIGHT there.
frontier.mechanism: Two blocks that differ only in content, with opposite scheduling outcomes, isolate the deciding quantity without any guessing about C spelling.
frontier.next_probe: Produce the same .sched / RANKDBG dump for func_8005D46C's first func_80073728 call block and diff the priority/class tables against func_80060544's Case3 block. Whatever differs IS the answer, and it converts directly into the C property to reproduce.

frontier.hypothesis: If the dumps show the a1 set-up is emitted late by expand_call rather than chosen late by the scheduler, the question is which C statement shape makes the second argument materialise earlier.
frontier.mechanism: expand_call emits argument register set-ups after the preceding statements' RTL, fixing their LUIDs; only a different source-level shape can move them, and s2 proved that respelling the argument itself is inert.
frontier.next_probe: Compare the pre-sched (.jump / .combine) RTL of the Case3 block against the sibling's, then, if they already differ there, use the sibling's C as the template. A permuter campaign is also cheap and extremely well-seeded now (base 2 with a matching instruction count) - follow [[permuter-fresh-seed-discipline]].
